name: jeroen blokland
zh_summary: @jsblokland: investing revolves around nominal returns, yet after one of the worst bond bear markets you must go back 30 years to find a positive cumulative real return on bonds.
en_summary: @jsblokland: investing revolves around nominal returns, yet after one of the worst bond bear markets you must go back 30 years to find a positive cumulative real return on bonds.
text:
It is rather remarkable that nearly everything in investing revolves around nominal returns.

Institutional investors determine their strategic asset allocation largely on the basis of nominal data.

Following one of the worst bond bear markets on record, you now have to go back 30 years to find a positive cumulative real return on bonds.

Many investors simply do not realize that three decades of real returns from bond investing have effectively been wiped out.

That does not mean bonds cannot perform well from here, especially now that real yields have turned positive again.

But if you were to use real returns in a standard mean-variance optimization model, as most institutional investors do, there is virtually no chance that bonds would receive an allocation anywhere near 40% in the strategic asset mix.

In fact, bonds receive no allocation at all once you expand the investment universe beyond different types of stocks and bonds.

And the outlook for bonds, something that is almost never incorporated into traditional mean-variance optimization models, becomes significantly less attractive when you factor in the prospect of higher inflation.

name: Sawyer Merritt
zh_summary: Disagrees with Marques Brownlee who says Tesla will never deliver the Rocket version of the new Roadster, as ordinary people won’t be able to buy it and it’s least important product. Thinks Tesla will deliver for depositors after years of development.
en_summary: Disagrees with Marques Brownlee who says Tesla will never deliver the Rocket version of the new Roadster, as ordinary people won’t be able to buy it and it’s least important product. Thinks Tesla will deliver for depositors after years of development.
text:
Marques Brownlee says Tesla will never deliver the Rocket version of their new Roadster:

“There’s no way you or I will be able to buy this car. We might as well ignore this becoming a real product. The base one, the fan car one, I can see that being possible. But at this point, I don’t even think it matters, because Tesla has proven to us that the Roadster is by far their least important product.”

I think Marques will be proven wrong, on all fronts. They didn’t spend years developing it to just not make it. While this new Roadster still has plenty of development work to go, the 2017 Roadster was much more of a prototype than this new one IMO. Tesla wants to deliver for all the people that put down deposit money all those years ago, and I think they will.

Weekly KAOS - The Monkey's Paw, the Hawkish Fed, and the Debt Governor

Many bellyache about the backup in yields to pre-GFC levels, but be careful what you wish for, because the most likely road to significantly lower rates runs through an economic and market BUST.

Welcome to the Weekly KAOS — UrbanKaoboy’s end-of-week roundup covering Macro and Geopolitics, where I try and tease out the most impactful bits of the week.

Themes of the Week
The Warsh Fed's recent hawkish lurch has caused many to bellyache about the backup in yields to levels last seen before the Global Financial Crisis, but the most likely road back to significantly lower rates runs straight through a potential economic and stock market Bust.

In the old W.W. Jacobs horror story, a family comes into a mummified Monkey’s Paw that grants three wishes, and the terror is that it grants each one in the cruelest way imaginable: they wish for money, and it arrives as the compensation check for their son, freshly killed in the machinery at the mill. I could not stop thinking about that this week, because the whole market seems to be quietly wishing the Warsh Fed back toward two or three percent Fed Funds, and as I posted on X, be careful what you wish for, because the likeliest path to rates that low is not a gentle glide but a brutal economic and market BUST. The Debt Governor is in charge now, and it’s the biggest threat to my hoped for Disinflationary Growth Goldilocks.
